body:
## 3-Line TL;DR

- GPT-6 Luna and Sol have lower standard input/output rates than Opus 5.5; that makes them worth trying on repeated work, not automatically cheaper per finished task
- My impression favors Sol and Luna on value and Opus 5.5 on finished output; this is a preference, not a controlled success-rate comparison
- Start with work you can check, cap retries and count every attempt; an inexpensive draft is less impressive when its editing department is you

## The rates are low. The unit matters

The comparison below uses USD per million tokens at standard API rates. OpenAI figures use the short-context tier; the illustrative total excludes caching and tool charges.

| Model | Input | Cache read | Output | 1m input + 250k output |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPT-6 Luna | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.50 | $0.225 |
| GPT-6 Sol | $2 | $0.20 | $10 | $4.50 |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | $4 | $0.20 | $20 | $9.00 |

*Sources: [OpenAI pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), [Anthropic pricing](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5/), checked September 27, 2026*

![Input and output API token rates for GPT-6 Luna, Sol, and Claude Opus 5.5](/images/posts/agi/gpt-6-api-prices.webp)

- The last column is a calculation across requests, not a single-request capacity or an estimate for your task: `input / 1m × input rate + output / 1m × output rate`
- At identical uncached usage, Sol costs half as much as Opus; their cache-read rate is equal, so the saving depends on the mix of fresh input, cached input and output
- Cache writes, tools, long-context tiers and processing modes can change the total; compare the settings you actually use, not whichever row makes your favorite model look frugal

## A cheap answer still has to finish the job

- A missed requirement can trigger another call, a larger conversation and manual repair; the original rate stays cheap while the task keeps getting more expensive
- Valid JSON is a format check, not a truth check; a perfectly placed bracket can surround a completely invented value
- That is why my favorable impression of Opus belongs beside the price table, not inside an imaginary benchmark. Better-looking output only becomes a cost advantage if it reduces actual rework

| Work | Candidate to try | Acceptance check |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Classification or fixed-field extraction | Luna | Required fields present, values supported by the source |
| A bounded code change | Luna or Sol | Relevant tests, complete requirements, no unrelated changes |
| Design or nuanced long-form writing | Compare Opus 5.5 too | Sound reasoning, no omissions, checked factual claims |

This is a proposed starting point, not a measured ranking. A task that is hard to check deserves more supervision even when the model sounds very pleased with itself.

![Acceptance checks, bounded retries, and escalation; all costs stay with the task](/images/posts/ai/acceptance-pipeline.webp)

## Count accepted work, including the ugly attempts

1. Pick recurring tasks and fix inputs, acceptance checks, tools and a retry limit before running the comparison
2. Log total API spend, accepted tasks, retries and human review minutes; keep failed attempts and escalation costs attached to the original task
3. Calculate **API cost per accepted task = total API spend / accepted tasks**; with zero accepted tasks, there is no useful unit cost
4. Compare review minutes separately, or convert them using the same hourly rate for every model

- If ten tasks cost $5 but only eight pass, the API cost is **$0.625 per accepted task**, not $0.50; this is an illustrative example, not a measured model result
- When the retry limit is reached, escalate or stop; asking one more time is a workflow choice, not a savings strategy by itself

## Community Reactions

- An r/OpenAI reporting-tool developer found omitted relevant items when comparing Luna 6 with Luna 5.6 at high effort. The issue was completeness, not merely whether the reply sounded helpful ([Reddit report](https://www.reddit.com/r/OpenAI/comments/1wnxg0n/luna_6_is_a_massive_downgrade_over_luna_56_misses/))
- An r/PiCodingAgent author reported Luna passing 29 of 30 runs across ten short coding tasks repeated three times, with automated verifiers. That supports trying bounded work in that setup; it does not establish a universal success rate ([Reddit benchmark](https://www.reddit.com/r/PiCodingAgent/comments/1wpcis6/opus_55_vs_gpt6_sol_luna_in_piagent_results_on_my/))

The reports concern different tasks and checks. The useful question is which resembles your workload, not which comment wins the model argument.

## Q&A (Field Notes)

- **Q: Does one failed Sol run erase its price advantage?**
  - Not automatically; two equal uncached runs match one Opus run at these rates, but actual token use and review effort need measuring
- **Q: Should a cache-heavy workflow always choose Opus?**
  - Equal cache-read rates alone cannot decide that; fresh input, output, cache writes and accepted-task counts still matter
- **Q: Can I use this table to choose a ChatGPT or Claude subscription?**
  - No; subscription allowances and API billing are separate products
title: GPT-6 Luna and Sol vs Opus 5.5: Cheap Tokens, Review Still Required
description: Comparing official API rates is easy. Comparing finished work takes retries, cache use and human review: where Luna, Sol and Opus 5.5 fit in a practical workflow.
imageAlt: Notebook comparing USD output token rates with retry and review costs
